title: Time Blindness: Now And Not-Now Are Your Only Two Times #Shorts
description: If you have ADHD, time does not feel like a timeline — it collapses into now or nowhere. This is called time blindness, and it explains why deadlines feel unreal until the last second, and why five minutes ago was actually forty. Common in ADHD, rooted in how the brain processes duration and future events. Follow for daily ADHD content.

voiceover: You pushed through for weeks. Now you can't get off the couch and you don't know why. That's not laziness — that's ADHD burnout, and it has a biological reason. ADHD brains run on dopamine and norepinephrine to sustain effort. When those are chronically depleted from masking, overcompensating, and white-knuckling through every task, your brain hits a hard floor. Not a soft tired — a full system shutdown. The crash feels like depression but it's depletion. And here's the trap: you rest, feel guilty, push harder, crash deeper. The cycle repeats. Breaking it takes three things: cut one non-essential obligation today — not eventually, today. Add one dopamine-restoring input that costs you nothing: sunlight for 10 minutes, one song you love, movement for 8 minutes. Then treat recovery as the actual work — because for your brain, right now, it is. Follow for daily ADHD content.
